newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks set record close, look to Budget.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks set record close, look to Budget.

text.p: SPI Futures 2547 +23 US 30yr cl 6.89 steady
10yrbond futs 92.340 +0.020 Gold NY 347.65 Lon fix 348.30
AUD US$0.7805 (Mon 0.7783) CRB Index cl 251.40 +1.87
*Stocks lock in early gains to end at record closing high, firm outlook overcomes Budget nerves. Vol 319.33 million, value A$754.20 million, 1114 stocks traded, 341 steady, 445 up, 328 down.
The Australian share market set closing and intraday record highs on Tuesday, taking its cue from another record run on Wall Street.
The All Ordinaries index added 9.5 points to close at 2,534.3, surpassing the previous record closing high of 2,526.0 set on May 9.
The benchmark index also registered a new intraday high of 2,540.4, toppling the previous record of 2,538.0 reached on Monday.
The June share price index futures were 23 points higher at 2,547, a 12.7 point premium to the underlying index.
"Everyone seems to expect a reasonably favourable result. Generally I don't think it is going to impact too greatly on our market," said a dealer at a Melbourne-based investment house.
Banks led the way to higher ground with half year profit expectations fueling three of the big four banks.

Westpac Banking Corp, which reports on Wednesday, was up eight cents to A$7.50 while sector leader National Australia Bank, due to report on Thursday, edged its way to another record high at A$18.35 before ending up 15.7 cents at A$18.337. ANZ Bank, which is due to report next week, climbed nine cents to A$8.49.

Regional bank St George Bank reported a sharply higher half year net profit of A$99.74 million and saw its shares jumped 13 cents to A$8.28, its highest level in six months, before profit takers succumbed to the temptation to cash in. St George shares ended the day square at A$8.15.
Oil/gas major Woodside Petroleum added 16 cents to end at A$10.86 after oil prices jumped offshore.

On the negative side, key industrials CSR and Amcor featured. CSR shares lost 13.3 cents to A$4.63 after the building materials, sugar and aluminium group reported a slump in full year net profit to A$212.2 million on Monday.

Sellers savaged paper and packaging giant Amcor after it issued a warning on second half profits, saying trading conditions remained difficult. Amcor was at a nine month high of A$8.75 prior to the warning but ended 18 cents down at A$8.45 on turnover of 2.5 million shares.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about seven to five, while about 31 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Futures trade was moderate but there remains a special "budget" trading session later today between 7.00 p.m. and 8.15 p.m. (0900 GMT and 1015 GMT).
The budget is to be handed down at 7.30 p.m. (0930 GMT).
Total options traded 30,774 (35,353)
Turnover in June SPI contracts totalled 5,926 (5,119)
In other local markets, Australian bond yields were slightly lower in fairly subdued trading ahead of the Federal budget.
By 5.00 p.m. (0700 GMT), 10 year T-bonds were yielding 7.64 percent, down from Monday's 7.66 percent.
The Australian dollar crept higher but lacked the momentum to escape its recent well worn range ahead of the budget.
By 5.00 p.m., the local dollar was in a holding pattern at US$0.7818/23 after gliding up from an early US$0.7789/94 and US$0.7775/80 late here Monday.
